title: Watch Becky G's First 'Vevo Official Live Performance' With '2AM' - antiMusic
content: (BHM) Vevo, the world's leading music video network, announces Becky G's 'Official Live Performance' of "2AM" from her album Baraja Bendita, out now. This release marks the first installment of an exclusive series of performance videos rolling out over the coming weeks. 'Official Live Performance' is Vevo's flagship original content franchise, which creates immersive, bespoke worlds for today's top artists to showcase their talent through the power of live performance. These productions are the result of deep creative synergy between Vevo, the artist and their team, and help artists connect with their global fanbases through exclusive visuals that are tailored to their album's unique vision. "Each song on Baraja Bendita really evokes a different kind of emotion, and I was able to channel that for each video in this project. I enjoyed expressing myself and transforming the space into something new for each song. I can't wait for fans to experience it in this new and unique way," says Becky G. "2AM" begins with Becky G's silhouette peeking through a foliage-covered rod iron gate. She enters into a peach-colored room draped with white curtains to sit on a vintage dark wood paneled dresser. Becky serenades listeners in her retreat away from any hustle and bustle as the camera pans around her before fading to black. Introducing various textures and elements from the wider space, the performance leaves viewers hungry to see what's beyond the walls of Becky's room. Becky G and Vevo previously worked together for a Vevo Footnotes video where she exclusively provides commentary break downs of the creation, lyrics, and meanings of some of her major hits including "Baile Con Mi Ex." "We're excited to have worked with Becky G, a trailblazing artist that not only brought so much passion to our shoot, but seamlessly blends genres and culture to empower her community and transform Latin music. Intimate and vulnerable, her performance makes you feel like a guest within Becky's home," says JP Evangelista, EVP of Content, Programming and Marketing, Vevo. "This video is a teaser to the bigger world of Baraja Bendita, with every video we're releasing in our series possessing an entirely unique vibe, choreography, lighting, and energy - much like the unexpected card dealt from a shuffled deck. Our team really translated each song into a fully realized live experience, culminating the series with a final short film for the album." title: G. S. Grewal Appointed President of Tractor and Mechanization Association (TMA) for 2026-28 - The Tribune
content:
New Delhi [India], August 15: The Tractor and Mechanization Association (TMA), the apex industry body representing India's tractor and farm mechanization sector, has appointed Mr. G. S. Grewal as its President for the 2026-28 term. The announcement was made during TMA's Annual General Meeting and Annual Business Session held in New Delhi. Mr. Grewal brings more than 36 years of experience in the tractor and agricultural machinery industry, with extensive leadership experience across sales, marketing, dealer development, customer support and business management. He currently serves as Chief Advisor at Escorts Kubota Limited and has previously served as Managing Director of Kubota Agricultural Machinery India. During his long association with the industry, Mr. Grewal has worked closely with customers, dealers, industry stakeholders and policymakers, giving him a broad perspective on the opportunities and challenges facing Indian agriculture and farm mechanization. "It is an honour to take on the responsibility of President of TMA. Indian agriculture is going through an important transformation, and farm mechanization will have an increasingly significant role in improving productivity, efficiency and sustainability. I look forward to working closely with TMA members, government, policymakers and other stakeholders to strengthen collaboration across the industry and support the changing needs of Indian farmers." As President, Mr. Grewal will focus on strengthening TMA's role as a platform for industry collaboration, constructive policy engagement, technology and innovation, sustainable mechanization, and the continued development of India's agricultural machinery ecosystem. "No association moves forward through one individual. Progress comes when the industry works together with a shared purpose. My endeavour will be to build on the work done by previous TMA leadership and further strengthen TMA as a collective voice for the tractor and farm mechanization industry." India is one of the world's largest tractor markets, while opportunities for broader farm mechanization continue to expand across crops, regions and farming applications. Increasing labour challenges, changing farming practices, emerging technologies and the need for sustainable agricultural solutions are expected to further increase the importance of mechanization in the years ahead. Under its new leadership, TMA will continue to work with its member companies and key stakeholders towards creating an enabling environment for the sustainable growth of the tractor and agricultural machinery industry. G. S. Grewal is a senior business leader with over 36 years of experience in the tractor and agricultural machinery industry. He currently serves as Chief Advisor at Escorts Kubota Limited and previously served as Managing Director of Kubota Agricultural Machinery India. He is passionate about leadership development, coaching and mentoring future leaders and is also the author of Leader as a Coach. The Tractor and Mechanization Association (TMA) represents leading manufacturers and stakeholders in India's tractor and agricultural mechanization industry. The Association works with industry, government and other stakeholders on issues relating to farm mechanization, technology, policy and the sustainable development of Indian agriculture. Following graduation of a highly successful group of seniors, Hart looks for the Titans’ Class of 2027 seniors to lead a relatively inexperienced to varsity football team that, following the program’s Maroon-and-Gold game at Jack Jewell Memorial Field Aug. 8, hosts Evansville Central Aug. 14 in an IHSAA preseason scrimmage ahead of the Titans’  season opener, a non-conference home game Aug. 21 against Class 5A-affiliated Floyd Central, which won the IHSAA Class 5A Sectional 16 title a year ago. They’ve really attacked this first week, which is great." “Even though we graduated a bunch of guys, we also have guys stepping up into new spots. We’ve got to keep getting better and fix some of the mistakes we’re making, but I feel like we’re ahead of where we thought we would be at this point of the season, so that’s always a good thing. With our schedule (which begins with playing 2025 5A Sectional Champion Floyd Central in Week 1 and Missouri powerhouse St. Pius X in Week 2 in the United Fidelity Bank Bowl), our guys are going to have to be ready to go right away.” “All summer, we’ve been working hard, and I thought we had a pretty good week one,” said Reinhart in describing the Titans’ preparations for the season ahead. “We’ve really been getting after it and competing throughout the summer and through week one,” added Campbell. “Yes, we graduated quite a few guys, but guys are working hard to step up and fill those roles. We’ve just got to continue to fight and improve so that we can be ready for Week 1.” As for this year's seniors, “They’ve exceeded my expectations, and they’ve really set the tone for our football team,” noted Hart. “They just go and attack every day and give it everything they have. Our seniors have done a really-great job so far.” Senior QB Caden Rochleau (22-for-41; 261 passing yards; 4 passing TD, 4 INT; 158 yards rushing, 1 rushing TD as a junior), after filling in for Wabash College football signee Zach Foster (197-for-310; 2164 yards passing, 29 TD passes, 10 INT; 1061 yards rushing; 9 rushing TD as a senior) following Foster’s injury in the regional championship game, made his first-career varsity start in the 2025 South Semi-State championship game and is set to fully take the reins of the Titans’ offense. “I couldn’t be more proud of Caden,” said Hart. “He’s stepped up and kind of taken that role head-on. He’s got all the talent in the world, and he’s done a great job of taking care of the football throughout the whole summer. I thought that in our first offensive drive (of the Maroon-Gold Game), he was surgical in the passing game and in the RPO game. He made great decisions and was getting the ball to where it needed to go. He was running our offense very well and very clinically. His understanding of the position, and his decision-making, continues to grow and progress.” “Caden’s really been getting after it all summer,” noted Reinhart. “He’s continued to step up and grow. He’s really committed to putting the work in and doing the best he can for our team so that we can be as successful as possible.” “Caden was thrown into a tough position (following the injury to Zach Foster), but he’s really worked his tail off to earn the position,” noted Campbell. “I’ve definitely seen growth in him. He’s determined, and he wants to win and help lead the team. It’s definitely a good mindset to have.” At running back, the Titans look to veteran backs in senior Eli Foster (378 yards rushing as a junior) and junior Tucker Deputy (274 yards rushing; 5 rushing TD as a sophomore) to fill the production provided by Hanover College football signee Colin Scherer (835 rushing yards; 14 rushing TD; 11 catches, 90 receiving yards as a senior), though Deputy has also transitioned into more of a role in the Gibson Southern linebacker corps. Others to watch include sophomore Makade Malone. “I think we’ve got a really nice stable there,” said Hart. “Eli brings a lot of experience and runs hard, and Makade Malone brings a speed factor to the backfield, and then we have Tucker, who ran it some last year. He’s more on the defensive side of things now, but we have the ability to bring him over, as well. We have three really-good guys back there to run the football for us.” “I think our run game has been solid so far,” added Reinhart. “Eli’s been pretty good, and he gives us a ton of experience in that spot. Overall, I think our running-back room is looking pretty good, which gives us confidence as an offensive line.” “I’m really happy Eli is there in the backfield,” said Campbell. “He’s a great fit at that position, and we feel confident that the rest of the room will continue to step up and grow.” With graduation of key contributors such as WR Noah Kuester (57 catches, 640 yards receiving, 13 TD receptions), WR/H-Back Toby Pullum (38 catches, 333 yards receiving, 6 TD receptions), WR Jake Mazzier (23 catches, 208 yards receiving, 1 TD reception) and WR Lloyd Sellers (28 catches, 394 yards receiving, 4 TD receptions), the Titans’ leading returning receiver is senior Peyton Johnson (42 catches; 483 yards receiving; 5 TD receptions as a junior). “Peyton’s had a great summer,” noted Hart. “He’s a guy that kind of gives us an A.J Brown-ish kind of receiver. He can take the top off of the defense and go get it, but as a big, strong, guy, he can break tackles and also give us those tough yards on the outside after catching hitches and curls.” Others to watch for in the receiving corps include juniors Ayden Bodrie and Luke Mallory, as well as senior Elijah Ortiz, junior Isaac Dill and junior Austin Smith. “Ayden and Luke are both very athletic and do a good job of going up and catching the football,” said Hart. “We’re looking to see who emerges and how that rotation works itself out.” “I feel like our receiving corps is going to be explosive and exciting this year,” described Reinhart. “They’ve all got big-play ability, especially with Caden’s arm strength. Peyton is back, and he was a big piece of our offense last year. We have a lot of guys competing for spots, which will be good for our team.” “Overall, I think our receivers are ready,” added Campbell. “Peyton is back, which is a big help. All the guys competing for those spots are ready to go.” While the Titans graduated three-fifths of last year’s offensive-line starters in LT Spencer Staggs, LG Blake Ulm and C Bobby Robinson, Gibson Southern returns starters in junior RG RJ Smith and senior RT Owen O’Neal to a new-look quintet in the trenches. Senior Ben Reinhart, who split time between tight end (5 catches, 39 yards in 2025) and defensive end (12 total tackles; 1 tackle for loss; 1 pass break-up - ahead of the Semi-State) as a junior, made the transition to serving as a full-time offensive lineman and looms at left tackle. Hart noted that competition is ongoing between the trio of Nathan Emery, Eli Bodrie and Jadyn Kiefer to determine who will emerge with the additional starting positions on the offensive line. “We’re continuing to get better there every single day,” said Hart. “Our pass protection is probably ahead of our run game at the moment. Over the next couple of weeks, we have to keep focusing on getting better up front in the run game. We had a couple of nice plays today, but we need to be able to run the football more efficiently and effectively than where we are after week one (of official practice).” “We graduated three guys on the left side of the line,” noted Reinhart, “but we get RJ and Owen back, which is huge for us. I kind of knew that I would be making the switch to the offensive line ahead of time. We also have a bunch of new guys that are hungry and looking to step up and earn those spots.” “The people that have filled in have stepped up to (try and) earn those positions,” added Campbell. “Guys are continuing to compete and fight for their spots. With who we have on the O-Line now, I feel like those guys are ready to go.” Following graduation of a senior-laden defense that featured Lindsey Wilson football signee and four-time All-State DT Brody Klem (65 total tackles; 28 TFL; 7 sacks; 1 forced fumble - ahead of the Semi-State), MLB Colin Scherer (116 total tackles; 10 TFL; 4 PBU; 2 INT; 2 fumble recoveries - ahead of the Semi-State) and DB Lloyd Sellers (state-leading 10 interceptions in 2025), the Titans look to a returning senior starter on each level in DT Khale Campbell (50 total tackles; 17 TFL; 5 sacks - ahead of the Semi-State - as a junior), LB Ian Maikranz (66 total tackles; 3 TFL; 1 INT; 4 PBU - ahead of the Semi-State - as a junior) and S Cole Ridens (59 total tackles; 4 PBU - ahead of the Semi-State - as a junior) to lead the way for a new-look group on that side of the football. Others competing for defensive-line spots alongside Campbell include senior DT Gavin McEllhiney, junior DT Isaac Peach, sophomore DE Lincoln Plasse and sophomore DE Reed Luecke. “It’s been great competition,” noted Reinhart of the Titans’ offensive and defensive lines competing against one another. “Iron sharpens iron, as I like to say. We push each other to play hard and make positive strides every day. We have guys on the D-Line that are hungry and looking to make an impact.” “We have some decent size up front, but I think overall as a defense, we’re a lot more athletic, maybe, than what we usually are,” noted Hart. “That’s something that really stands out. Those guys are really able to run around and chase things down. As a whole, our defense flies around and makes plays. It’s a group that I’m really excited about. This is a group that, throughout the summer and through week one, has been able to run the ball particularly well on us. We still have some work to do, but our front-seven has done a really good job of playing the run so far.” “We have some younger guys on the line,” noted Campbell, “but they have the right mindset of doing what it takes to win. We’ve been attacking every day in practice, and we’re ready to just go, go, go.” As for the Titans’ linebacker corps, “Ian played outside last year, but we’ve moved him to ‘Mike’ this year, and he’s done a great job in there,” noted Hart. “He’s been the quarterback of the defense for us and gets us where we need to be. “Tucker Deputy has moved over from running back, and then junior Gabe Foster and junior Max Brink are competing, as well,” Hart added. “As a whole, our linebackers have played really well. I really like where we are there in terms of athleticism. That group is possibly as athletic a group that we’ve had there in a while from a strength and speed standpoint. They do a great job of flying around.” “Ian has stepped up, and that group as a whole is really going and competing on every play,” noted Campbell. “They’re doing their jobs well and getting their jobs done.” “Those guys are battling every day and continuing to get better,” said Reinhart of the linebacker corps. The Titans’ secondary team is battling through various injuries ahead of the 2026 campaign, said Hart. “It’s been a mix-and-match type of thing there so far,” Hart said. “Cole Ridens is back as a starter at safety, and Elijah (Ortiz) played a lot of safety last year, as well. Having two guys at safety with that level of experience is huge.” At cornerback, “Isaac Dill started a couple of games last year,” added Hart. “(Junior) Eli Stone and (junior) Kaigan Nossett have also done a fantastic job so far. We’ve got a little depth there. “As a whole, and as a team, there are some guys that have stepped up over the summer and through this first week that we weren’t sure were going to get there,” Hart said. “We have to keep building competitive depth across the board, especially with the way that we want to play. A lot of guys have continued to step up and work hard as we go into the season.” “I’m really proud of those guys. The guys in the secondary are really competing and fighting to earn their spots,” noted Campbell. “I feel like we’re pretty strong in the secondary.” Rochleau returns as the team’s punter, but the competition for the remainder of the Titans’ special teams’ positions is ongoing following the graduation of senior PK Will Redden (59-for-61 PATs, 3-for-5 FGs in 2025), a three-sport All-Gibson County athlete a year ago (football, soccer and golf), as well as Mazzier, a Western Kentucky University Baseball signee and the 2025-26 Princeton Clarion Gibson County Male Athlete of the Year, who played a key role in the return game in 2025. Hart noted that Jeter Simmons, a Princeton Clarion All-Gibson County and All-Pocket Athletic Conference performer on the soccer pitch, looms as the team’s kicker in filling that role in a similar fashion to what Redden did a season ago. “Jeter is new to us, and he had a good day today (Saturday at the Maroon-Gold Game), where he didn’t miss one, which I thought was great” noted Hart. “For a guy that’s never really kicked before (on the football field), he’s really been consistent throughout the opening week. He’s come out and has done a great job." “Jeter’s stepped up and earned that position,” noted Campbell. “He’ll be ready to go.” “Caden’s got a great leg as our punter,” shared Hart. “He’s an athletic guy, and it’s always good to have a guy that is as athletic as him as your punter. He did a great job last year, and he’s continued to do a great job so far there.” Lincoln Plasse, who has been “really consistent so far here, early in the process,” said Hart, looms as the team’s long snapper, while Elijah Ortiz looms as a candidate to return punts, while Isaac Dill and Makade Malone loom as potential candidates as kickoff returners. Special teams “is something that we spend a lot of time on and want to be good at, although it’s maybe the toughest thing to simulate and get a good live look at at this point of the year,” said Hart. “We won’t fully know what we have there until we get into that Week One game. Through the first week (of official practice), I really like where we are in the kicking game.” “It starts up front in the trenches on both sides of the ball,” said Reinhart in describing the keys to the Titans having success in 2026. “If we want to be successful, we have to dominate up front.” “We’ve just got to keep going, keep driving and putting in the work every day,” concluded Campbell. “We’ve got to keep building and getting better each day,” concluded Hart, “and we need to make sure, as we go along with the season, that we have guys continue to step up and play at a high level, week-in and week-out. We’re going to compete. This group will always compete really hard. We’re going to find out right away where we stand. We’re going to keep diving into the details as we work to play to the best of our ability.” Follow us on X/Twitter: @pdcprepsports and @Coach_Kyle_Hill Keep it Clean. NASA will hold a two-day aerospace exposition this November, and it may draw a surprising number of "Simpsons" fans. The event, which NASA announced today (Aug. 14), will be held Nov. 7 and Nov. 8 at Kennedy Space Center (KSC) on Florida's Space Coast. It's called "Max Power," which is also a famous Homer Simpson pseudonym. In the 13th episode of the show's 10th season, which first aired in February 1999, Homer legally changed his name to Max Power. He wanted to disassociate himself from a bumbling character on the (fictional) TV show "Police Cops" who shared his given moniker. Homer made the switch to Max Power — which he said he got off a hair dryer — without consulting his family, a move that did not go over well. "Wait a minute!" his dad protested. "The family name is my legacy to you. I got it from my father, and he got it from his father, and he traded a mule for it. And that mule went on to save spring break." "But I fell in love with Homer Simpson," she said. "I don't want to snuggle with Max Power." "Nobody snuggles with Max Power," Homer — or rather Max — responded. "You strap yourself in and feel the Gs!" NASA's Max Power expo is about feeling the Gs as well, at least in part. "The two-day event will feature immersive experiences for all ages to enjoy, including air shows, skydiving stunts, technology demonstrations, spaceflight hardware, military aircraft and behind‑the‑scenes access to America's spaceport," agency officials wrote in a description of the expo. "Attend talks led by NASA experts and meet astronauts from some of agency’s most famous missions!" NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, an accomplished pilot as well as a private astronaut, said that he plans to participate in the expo's air show. And, if you're unable to attend this November, you'll likely have other chances down the road. "Certainly, the idea is that this event, Max Power, becomes the first of many," Isaacman said during a press conference today. title: Becky G's collaboration with Selena Gomez was totally unplanned - contactmusic.com
content: MUSIC NEWS FROM AROUND THE WORLD Becky G has revealed that her "surreal" collaboration with Benny Blanco and Selena Gomez on the track Te Olvido (La La) came about unintentionally. Becky G's collaboration with Benny Blanco and Selena Gomez came about by accident. The 29-year-old singer teamed up with the husband-and-wife duo on the new track Te Olvido (La La) and explained that the song was completely unplanned. Becky G told Rolling Stone: "It's just everything. I was trippin'. The Gomez girls, finally! She's the sweetest. "And I've known Benny for so long now, which is crazy. I remember the day we went into the studio, again, no intention set, just kind of like: 'Let's create and let's see what happens' "And I feel like it was a few weeks after, the song was so stuck in my head. I literally would wake up like: 'La, la, la la la, la, la, la, la la.' "And I'd walk around my house, and then I'd text my manager Ben, then I hit Benny, and be like: 'OK, so what are we gonna do with this song? What's gonna happen with the song?' And it just continued to unfold." She went on to add: "I remember hearing Sel's verse on it, and hearing our voices together was so surreal. And then we shot our music video. "And it was so wild, because I shot the EPA music video around the same time. "Literally it was like a three-day span where we had shot the EPA music video and then we also did our music video. Everybody's like: 'Damn, Becky's really out here. What's going on? Like we wanna know the tea.' The collaboration with Gomez comes after Becky confessed she doesn't see other female artists as competition. The Shower singer - who has a particularly close friendship with Karol G - has revealed she hates it when female artists are pitted against each other. Speaking about her relationship with the Provenza singer, Becky told CBS Mornings: "We have a beautiful friendship, one I’m really, really thankful for, and one that I think throughout the years, we’ve really earned with one another. "I think that’s for many, many reasons … through experiences, shared experiences, individual experiences and, of course, an industry that is so quick to pit people against each other." Becky scoffed at the idea that Karol is an adversary. Asked if they're rivals, she said: "Absolutely not. No. "I mean, for me, personally, my greatest competition is the person I look at in the mirror every morning, you know? And I know she feels the same way for herself. "Our goal is to be the best versions of ourselves, and it’s been beautiful to kind of grow up in this friendship as well, and see someone literally just not only break down every door, but also hold it open for others to come through."

title: The Adventure Bike That Owners Keep Longer Than Expected - Top Speed
content: Abhik has been an automotive journalist for over a decade, with expertise in both motorcycle and car road testing, reviewing, as well as writing and executing feature travelogs. He has worked for Indian brands including Evo India Magazine, Auto Today by India Today Group, and anchored video reviews for Powerdrift Studios. He also has keen interests in most forms of motorsports, having competed in a couple of seasons of one-make racing with TVS Racing on two wheels and Volkswagen Motorsport on four. Alongside his motoring pursuits, e-sports and sim racing are current interests, as are cycling and cycling tech. Today’s tech-led motorcycling world is so fast-paced that model progression year-on-year can not just be quick, but also jump forward substantially. Honda proved as much with a single-generation swap where the 2019 CRF1000L Africa Twin was replaced by the CRF1100L in 2020, which was leaps and bounds forward in tech. It came with a higher 1,084cc displacement, a six-axis IMU, and a touchscreen. What this does is create a buyer response of wanting the latest and greatest rather than sticking to the older model, which would still serve for years mechanically. But every now and then, a product comes along that challenges established norms, and a BMW flagship adventure bike sets the example of one. Switching bikes costs more than money. Romanticizing the love for motorcycles is one thing, but a pragmatic perspective will tell you that a rider who has logged a decent number of miles on one machine has spent ample time with it to have subconsciously calibrated its nuances. And these are details that are now muscle memory. Stuff like how much front brake force the fork takes up before the nose dives aggressively, and exactly where the pegs touch down through a tight corner to have a mental map of the bike's grip limits. A new bike may be mechanically different, and these nuances take a bit of a learning curve to establish again. The learning curve is a non-issue, and is what helps you build skills in a motorcycling discipline of choice. It’s the findings that may lead to a mental comparison and the possible regret of getting a new machine that doesn’t live up to the old one. For some riders, especially those who spend a lot of saddle time traversing unforgiving terrains where support or help can be scarce, these factors matter more than the latest tech on offer. The trust and knowledge of a bike well established in the rider’s mind are what prevent one from scratching the itch for a new bike. In the ADV space, there’s only one bike that resonates with this logic. At $17,995 to start, the BMW R 1250 GS wasn't cheap when BMW sold it new between 2019 and 2023, before the R 1300 GS pushed it out of the current lineup. Used listings today run closer to $13,700 to $16,000, depending on mileage and options. But it’s not the great resale value that makes owners hold onto the bike. Underneath, a 1,254cc boxer twin uses BMW's ShiftCam variable valve timing that’s good for 136 hp and 105 lb-ft, output that hasn't aged into irrelevance despite a five-year-old engine. Riders who bought one when it was new are, in plenty of cases, still riding it and there are yet more reasons why. BMW's ShiftCam variable valve timing is what makes that output possible, switching cam profiles depending on specific load and rpm. But the ownership costs are what make the R 1250 GS all the more appealing. Valve clearance rarely needs correcting even after 100,000 kilometers on this engine, and mechanics who've opened one up at that mileage report pistons, cylinders, and the crankshaft all still looking relatively factory-fresh. BMW calls for an inspection of the shaft drive at 12,500 miles and swaps it out preventively around 37,000, even footing that replacement bill itself for as long as the owner keeps the bike. That’s a huge plus in itself. A boxer engine and a drivetrain that both hold up that well simply don't give an owner a reason to trade in the bike on mechanical grounds alone. BMW’s unique telelever front end, something you’ll often hear GS owners brag about, soaks up 7.5 inches of travel through a design BMW has refined since the 1990s. It trades the dive of a conventional fork for a setup that stays composed under hard braking no matter the model year. Chassis composure aside, the electronics are still current. Standard equipment included a 6.5-inch TFT display, a full LED headlight, and Hill Start Control, along with two riding modes, Rain and Road. An optional Riding Modes Pro package added Dynamic, Dynamic Pro, Enduro, and Enduro Pro, offering six settings in total. It’s no wonder then that the R 1250 GS is still highly regarded as the ultimate ADV. Another reason that the R 1250 GS is preferred as a used buy is that BMW never sold the R 1250 GS as a single, fixed setup. Seat height ranges from a standard 33.5 to 34.3 inches down to 31.5 to 32.3 inches with the factory low-suspension option, and BMW offered a wider spread of factory seat heights on top of that. So a younger rider who has the flexibility to tolerate a taller seat may only have to switch saddles and/or suspension 10 or 15 years down the line, instead of switching bikes altogether. At 476 pounds, the weight is still manageable with room for a passenger, a full set of panniers, and a top case. BMW has even gone ahead and thought of making things easier for the rider with the optional Dynamic ESA electronic suspension. It adjusts on the fly, softening up for a loaded touring run and firming back up for a solo commute. And this is what makes the R 1250 GS so versatile for speed, comfort and everyday use if so desired. A 2017 Triumph Tiger Explorer 1200 undercuts the GS on the used market, typically running around $9,540. Its 1,215cc inline-triple makes 137 horsepower and 89 lb-ft, more of both than the boxer twin, and a shaft final drive keeps its own maintenance low the same way the GS's does. What it can't match is the GS's specific legacy and pedigree for round-the-world travel. The GS, after all, defined adventure riding for the modern motorcyclist. A brand new 2026 Harley-Davidson Pan America 1250 Special is the kind of bike that makes a five-year-old GS feel old on paper. It starts at $19,999, and its 1,252cc Revolution Max V-twin makes 150 horsepower and 94 lb-ft, wrapped in a platform that didn't exist when the R 1250 GS was already several years into production. That's exactly the pitch aimed at a GS owner shopping for something newer. The Pan America has only been on sale since 2021, though; it isn't much time to build the kind of ownership history the GS enjoys. Both rivals pull in a different direction, with the Tiger on long-distance capability and the Pan America being newer and stronger on paper. But neither can borrow the GS's sheer globe-trotting legacy, and the long-distance trips that built the name or the high-mileage ownership culture that keeps this generation off the used lots and in their owners’ garages longer than most. title: Becky G's new album 'marries' both sides of her personality - Female First
content: Becky G's new album reflects both sides of her personality. The 29-year-old singer has just released Baraja Bendita, her fifth studio album, and Becky feels proud of the record because it's honest to every side of her personality. The chart-topping star - whose real name is Rebbeca Gomez - told CBS Mornings: "I feel like this album really marries the Rebbecca side of me ... the sensual, more vulnerable side of me, the intimate side of me, and then also, you know, who I am. "The boss in the boardroom and the boss on the stage." Becky's album title loosely translates to, a blessed deck of cards. And the singer claims that she's "gotten really good at playing the game" during the course of her career. She said: "We all know that quote of we can't necessarily control the cards that we were dealt – but what we can control is how we play them. "I feel like throughout my years of, of doing what I do, personally and professionally, I've gotten really good at playing the game and I think that that's something that especially as women, as we've become more empowered, we're almost taught to feel more shameful about that and I think I'm just owning it." Becky previously admitted to feeling isolated during the early years of her music career. The singer - who was born to American parents of Mexican descent - recalled being the "youngest" and the "only brown girl in the room" at various points in her career. Becky - who released her debut album, Mala Santa, in 2019 - told Interview magazine: "This industry can be very lonely, and sometimes I really crave a connection with people who really understand what it is to be in my shoes. "For so long, I was the youngest person, or the only woman, or the only brown girl in the room. I felt isolating. So finding artists who understand the hard work and sacrifice that comes with success makes all of it feel more meaningful."

title: Between the F 450 GS and the F 900 GS: BMW’s new mid-range GS is coming in 2028 - SPEEDWEEK.com
content: Following the entry-level class comes the mid-range segment: a 600-cc touring enduro bearing the legendary ‘GS’ designation and featuring an in-line twin engine will enable BMW to target new customer groups. This article is an automatically generated English version. The original article was published in German. Special anniversary exhibition: Swiss Museum of Transport in Lucerne showcases Ducati’s history 10,000 PS and 500 km/h: 3 days of drag racing action at the Hockenheimring Now including exhaust systems: WP Pro Components expands its product range Four weeks ago, Aprilia headed into the summer break from Germany with a badly injured Marco Bezzecchi. The response came from the heart of British motor racing: ‘Together we are strong!’ SPEEDWEEK.com readers had known this for some time: a few weeks before BMW unveiled its new entry-level range, the F 450 GS, in Milan, BMW Motorrad boss Markus Flasch had already hinted, in a conversation with editor-in-chief Ivo Schützbach, that the Bavarian development engineers would be taking another close look at the new F 450 platform for the next expansion of the model range. As we were also able to report for the first time shortly afterwards, this new iteration of the parallel-twin engine will debut in a lightweight touring enduro, with which BMW is targeting customers of Yamaha’s best-selling Ténéré 700 and will be bringing the legendary ‘GS’ designation into a new market segment. Initial photos of an early test prototype now reveal for the first time the approach the Bavarian manufacturer intends to take to make its mark in the segment between the F 450 GS and the F 900 GS: The touring enduro shows clear technical parallels with the F 450 GS and draws on a similar approach for the exhaust system and chassis components. The rear shock absorber mounting, for example, is similar to that of its little sister, and the swingarm is of a similar design. Yet the differences are also clear: the motorbike is fitted with a 21-inch front wheel and an 18-inch rear wheel, and looks considerably more grown-up than its by no means petite little sister. The steel bridge frame on the prototype is also more closely modelled on the F 900 GS, and the braking system resembles that of its big sister. The fairing parts also reveal that the bike is still at an early stage of development, yet many design details are already finely crafted. For instance, the headlight will apparently be modelled on that of its big sister, the R 1300 GS, although the characteristic ‘beak’ is still missing. At the same time, the design details that are still missing reveal that development is far from complete. The name is also still up in the air: ‘F 600 GS’ would fit into the BMW nomenclature, whilst a revival of the ‘F 650 GS’ or ‘F 700’ designations would also be a logical possibility. In any case, actual engine capacity would not be a determining factor for the name: the F 800 and F 900 GS, for example, use the same engine and therefore have the same cylinder capacity. Special anniversary exhibition: Swiss Museum of Transport in Lucerne showcases Ducati’s history 10,000 PS and 500 km/h: 3 days of drag racing action at the Hockenheimring Now including exhaust systems: WP Pro Components expands its product range On the subject of engine capacity: “Something bigger” is on the cards for the new mid-range model compared to the F 450 GS, as BMW Motorrad CEO Markus Flasch hinted during a conversation with us at the time – the engine still has “reserves”. That’s not very specific, but a look at the current BMW model range reveals a large gap between 420 and 895 cubic centimetres of displacement, and a look at BMW’s partner TVS also helps. The Indian company manufactures the F450 range on behalf of BMW and has also just brought a bored-out version of the parallel-twin to production for the ‘Atlas’ from its British subsidiary Norton, thereby demonstrating the development potential of the engine. In the Indo-British variants, the Atlas and Atlas GT, the BMW engine – in a heavily revised form – delivers a displacement of 585 cubic centimetres and 70 PS. Four weeks ago, Aprilia headed into the summer break from Germany with a badly injured Marco Bezzecchi. The response came from the heart of British motor racing: ‘Together we are strong!’ The engine in BMW’s mid-range GS differs from that of the Norton in several respects in our photos, whilst others show similarities. The internal workings will certainly differ: the British model, for example, uses a crankshaft with the 270-degree ignition offset typical of this class, whilst the BMW F450 GS employs an unorthodox 135-degree crankpin offset. Reportedly, the displacement of the BMW and Norton is said to be on a par, and the rated power output is also likely to be comparable, depending on the final design of the engine: This would mean between 65 and 70 PS for the Bavarian model, placing it just below the class benchmark, the Yamaha Ténéré 700. Last but not least, there is the question of the launch date: the test bike shows that BMW still has some development work to do on the new mid-range GS. A launch is therefore not expected before 2028. title: Becky G's collaboration with Selena Gomez felt 'surreal' - Female First
content: Becky G's collaboration with Selena Gomez and Benny Blanco felt "surreal". Becky G has opened up about working with Selena Gomez The 29-year-old singer teamed up with the pair on new track Te Olvido (La La) and she's now revealed the project came about by accident after she created the song and she felt thrilled to hear her voice alongside Selena's in the final edit. Becky G told Rolling Stone: "It's just everything. I was trippin'. The Gomez girls, finally! She's the sweetest. "And I've known Benny for so long now, which is crazy. I remember the day we went into the studio, again, no intention set, just kind of like: 'Let's create and let's see what happens' "And I feel like it was a few weeks after, the song was so stuck in my head. I literally would wake up like: 'La, la, la la la, la, la, la, la la.' "And I'd walk around my house, and then I'd text my manager Ben, then I hit Benny, and be like,: 'OK, so what are we gonna do with this song? What's gonna happen with the song?' And it just continued to unfold." She went on to add: "I remember hearing Sel's verse on it, and hearing our voices together was so surreal. And then we shot our music video. "And it was so wild, because I shot the EPA music video around the same time. "Literally it was like a three-day span where we had shot the EPA music video and then we also did our music video. Everybody's like: 'Damn, Becky's really out here. What's going on? Like we wanna know the tea.' It comes after Becky confessed she doesn't see other female artists as competition. The singer - who has a particularly close friendship with Karol G - has revealed she hates it when female artists are pitted against each other. Speaking about her relationship with Karol, Becky told CBS Mornings: "We have a beautiful friendship, one I’m really, really thankful for, and one that I think throughout the years, we’ve really earned with one another. "I think that’s for many, many reasons … through experiences, shared experiences, individual experiences and, of course, an industry that is so quick to pit people against each other." Becky rubbished the idea that Karol is a rival, insisting she doesn't view other female artists through that lens. Asked if they're rivals, Becky said: "Absolutely not. No. "I mean, for me, personally, my greatest competition is the person I look at in the mirror every morning, you know? And I know she feels the same way for herself. "Our goal is to be the best versions of ourselves, and it’s been beautiful to kind of grow up in this friendship as well, and see someone literally just not only break down every door, but also hold it open for others to come through."

title: GS Global spurs North American energy sector with new Houston office - The Korea Times
content: From left, GS Global U.S. President Lee Jun-hak, Jindal Pipe U.S. President Vikas Chandra, Korean Consul General in Houston Lee Kyung-eun, GS Global Corp. Head of Steel Department and Senior Vice President Kim Jung-hoon, Brown Strauss President and CEO Kris Farris and GS Global U.S. Houston Branch General Manager Park Jun-hee join a ribbon-cutting event during the opening ceremony for  GS Global Houston Branch in the United States, Tuesday (local time). Courtesy of GS Global Energy and infrastructure accelerator GS Global has opened a new branch in Houston, strengthening its local sales capabilities as it targets growing opportunities in North America’s energy and infrastructure markets. The company held an opening ceremony on Tuesday (local time) in Uptown, one of Houston’s major commercial districts. Attendees included Korean Consul General in Houston Lee Kyung-eun, representatives from key customers such as Jindal USA and major Korean and international companies including POSCO, Hyundai Steel, Korea National Oil Corporation and Hanwha Ocean. The establishment of the Houston branch reflects GS Global’s strategic decision to respond proactively to rising demand for project-based steel products driven by increased investment in energy, power generation and infrastructure across the United States. Demand for high-quality steel products has expanded particularly rapidly as construction of artificial intelligence data centers and investment in power infrastructure accelerate nationwide. GS Global has been operating its U.S. business primarily through its Los Angeles-based subsidiary. However, amid strengthened protectionist trade policies and the ongoing restructuring of global supply chains, the company decided to establish an additional base in Houston, a key hub for the U.S. energy industry. The Houston branch will go beyond importing and selling steel products. Its key responsibilities will include identifying demand for project-based steel, supporting project acquisition, participating in the U.S. energy industry’s value chain and expanding into related business areas such as energy, chemicals and shipbuilding equipment. The branch also plans to maximize cooperation with major Korean steelmakers that have operations near Houston, including Hyundai Steel and Dongkuk Steel. It will also seek new business partners among local engineering, procurement and construction companies and steel fabricators. During the second half of this year, GS Global will focus on establishing local networks, strengthening project pipeline management and stabilizing the branch’s operations. Beginning in 2027, it plans to expand project acquisition support and identify new business opportunities, with the goal of developing the Houston branch into a core hub for business development in the southern U.S. “Establishing the Houston branch is a strategic investment aimed at expanding our contact points with customers in the U.S. market and strengthening our practical sales capabilities,” a GS Global representative said. “We will identify diverse new opportunities, including project-based steel businesses, and establish a sustainable foundation for growth in North America.” With the opening of the Houston branch, GS Global now operates a global network of 23 overseas offices and entities across 16 countries. In the U.S., the company will enhance its market responsiveness through its Los Angeles subsidiary and the new Houston branch.

Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Leader of Opposition in the Assembly R Ashoka said the BJP and JD(S) had decided to boycott the Speaker election in protest against the ruling Congress "unconstitutionally" naming the new Speaker on its official letterhead. He accused the Congress of starting a new tradition in the country and the State by announcing the Speaker's name on its party letterhead, thereby undermining the sovereignty of the House and the rights of its elected representatives. He was referring to the Congress high command's letter to CM D. K. Shivakumar on August 3, which contained the names of 19 ministers to be inducted into his Cabinet. The letter also contained the names of the party's nominees for the post of Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Assembly, Chairperson, and Deputy Chairperson of the Council. Mr. Ashok had also made it clear that once the Speaker was elected, the BJP and JD(S) would accord the Speaker's chair and office all due respect. title: 12 BMW Motorcycles Worth Every Penny - Top Speed
content: In the American motorcycle market, BMW Motorrad offers one of the most diverse lineups of bikes. These range from luxury tourers to do-it-all adventure bikes to retro-vibing roadsters and track-going monsters. At the same time, BMW surprisingly keeps the value quotient in check (particularly from a European bikemaker context), and most of its bikes are worth each penny you pay. We're talking about 12 such bikes, ranging from touring bikes with Japanese reliability to adventure bikes that excel at everything. There's something for everyone here. BMW offers the best of two-wheeled luxury, comfort, and performance with the K 1600 GTL. This full dresser brings the best of "big" American luxury charm with sophisticated technology to offer a surprisingly versatile land yacht. A unique six-cylinder engine powers the K 1600 GTL. This 1,649 cc mill produces 160 horsepower at 6,750 RPM and 132.7 pound-feet at 5,250 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual coupled to a final shaft drive system. For the chassis, a cast-aluminum bridge-type frame is present. It is suspended on BMW's famed Duolever front suspension with a central spring strut and 4.5 inches of travel. The rear gets the Paralever setup, coupled to a cast-iron single-sided swingarm and 5.3 inches of travel. Technology features are galore, too. Notable ones include a huge 10.25-inch TFT, a four-button cluster for custom functions, dynamic traction control, three ride modes, dynamic electronic suspension, hill start control, heated grips and seats, and an audio system, among others. This is arguably the most value-packed luxury touring motorcycle, and it undercuts the Honda Gold Wing, despite being more powerful. The 1,649 cc mill mentioned above is present here as well, in the same exact tune. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual and a final shaft drive neatly hidden in its single-sided swingarm. The chassis is also similar to the GTL, featuring the bridge-type cast aluminum frame. As for suspension, the front gets a double-wishbone (Duolever) with 4.5 inches of travel. The rear gets a monoshock (Paralever) setup with 5.3 inches of travel. The suspension offers electronic adjustability and even an automatic load-leveling feature. There is no dearth of top-spec technology. The K 1600 B gets a huge 10.25-inch TFT with a wide range of connectivity and integrated map navigation features. Other notable features include three ride modes, dynamic traction control, hill start control, and engine brake control, among others. It makes for a first-class touring experience that will have you looking forward to every touring opportunity. It’s powered by a big boxer engine that delivers at least 110 pound-feet of torque between 2,000 and 4,000 RPM. Other touring bits include a relaxed riding posture, a massive fairing with deflectors, high-quality saddlebags and a topcase with available central locking, and available active cruise control. It also gets a large TFT display paired with 4 traditional analog gauges, with an available Marshall sound system. It’s a unique German take on a formula that’s otherwise very American. Also, the Pope has one! This futuristic-looking touring bike makes luxury feel practical. The same boxer twin powers the R 1300 RT as on the go-anywhere R 1300 GS. The 1,300 cc mill produces 145 horsepower at 7,750 RPM and 110 pound-feet of torque at 6,500 RPM, sent to the wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox coupled to a final Cardan shaft drive system for added durability. Adding to its versatility is a factory-adjustable seat, solid wind protection, and commendable technology. Notable features include keyless ride, dynamic electronic stability control, heated grips, and a gorgeous-looking 10.25-inch TFT with Bluetooth navigation as standard. The banking industry is witnessing a structural shift toward active ETFs and options-based income products, as investors increasingly seek higher income, tax efficiency and downside-risk management within the liquid ETF wrapper. Derivative-income ETFs have grown to roughly $180 billion in assets, seeing a CAGR of more than 70% since 2021, according to Goldman's official press release citing Morningstar. Against this backdrop, The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. GS has agreed to acquire NEOS Investments for consideration of up to $2.25 billion in cash and equity, subject to certain performance and service commitments. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, pending regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. The acquisition will add $30 billion in assets across NEOS' 19 options-based income ETFs to Goldman Sachs Asset Management's existing $40 billion in income and outcome-oriented options-based ETF solutions. Once complete, the deal will make Goldman Sachs Asset Management the eighth-largest active ETF provider. The NEOS purchase follows Goldman's acquisition of Innovator Capital Management, and together the deals create a broad options-based ETF franchise spanning buffer, managed outcome and income strategies. As of June 30, 2026, Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Innovator from Goldman Sachs Asset Management and NEOS manage more than $130 billion in ETF assets under supervision. Overall, Goldman Sachs' push into options-based ETFs is likely to enhance its competitive advantage by giving the firm greater scale, a broader range of differentiated products and stronger exposure to fast-growing active ETF categories. The addition of NEOS, alongside Innovator, strengthens Goldman's presence across income, buffer and managed-outcome strategies, helping it compete more effectively for investor assets. At the same time, the expansion should support higher recurring fee revenues and further diversify its Asset & Wealth Management business. Competition has been intensifying for Goldman as banks like Morgan Stanley MS and JPMorgan JPM are expanding crypto-related capabilities even if they have not yet launched proprietary ETFs. Morgan Stanley has filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to launch ETFs linked to Bitcoin and Solana. The proposed products — the Morgan Stanley Bitcoin Trust and the Morgan Stanley Solana Trust — are designed to give investors direct price exposure to the two cryptocurrencies without requiring them to own or store the tokens themselves. JPMorgan has taken a broader, infrastructure-led approach to crypto and blockchain. The bank offers crypto trading services to institutional clients and has built out custody capabilities, while also piloting on-chain settlement and tokenized deposits through its blockchain unit, Onyx. JPMorgan has launched blockchain-based platforms for wholesale payments and repo transactions, enabling faster and more efficient settlement using tokenized assets. title: State Department expands push to reclassify employees as at-will workers - Government Executive
content:
The State Department is expanding its search for employees to reclassify as at-will workers under the Trump administration’s new Schedule Policy/Career designation
                  
                    J. David Ake/Getty Images The State Department is taking another look at its workforce to see if more employees should fall under a new governmentwide designation that makes them easier to fire. Agency officials are expanding their search for employees to reclassify as at-will workers under the Trump administration’s new Schedule Policy/Career designation for the federal workforce. President Donald Trump signed an executive order in June that officially reclassified 8,000 federal employees into Schedule Policy/Career, a rebranding of the Schedule F designation that Trump pursued in his first term, but did not implement before leaving office. Employees placed into the new schedule would no longer be able to challenge adverse personnel actions before the Merit Systems Protection Board, and whistleblower complaints filed by Schedule P/C employees would be investigated by their own agency, rather than the Office of Special Counsel. The Office of Personnel Management previously estimated that about 50,000 federal employees would fall under this new job category. But an OPM spokesperson said in June that the administration chose to instead focus on “the most senior-level career policy officials.” The State Department’s actions suggest that its initial reclassification of employees fell short of the White House’s expectations, and other agencies may take a similar approach. NOTUS first reported that the Trump administration is directing agencies to find more federal employees to convert to Schedule P/C. A spokesperson for the foreign policy agency declined to comment on “internal deliberative personnel matters.” One State Department employee told Government Executive that human resources officials are using a short questionnaire to determine if GS-13 and GS-14 level employees are working in policymaking positions that should be reclassified to Schedule P/C. “It is not clear how many ‘yes’ responses would trigger a new Schedule P/C status,” the employee said. The questionnaire asks if a position “formulates, develops and/or determines foreign policy, including creation of draft documents with policy recommendations," or "develops or reviews non-public Executive Orders, regulations, directives, policy memoranda, or deliberative materials protected by the deliberative process privilege regarding foreign policy." Other screening questions ask if an employee “provides substantive advocacy of foreign policy,” or represents the department before Congress, the Office of Management and Budget, foreign governments or external organizations regarding the administration’s foreign policy. The questionnaire asks if an employee “publicly advocates Administration foreign policy through official communications or media engagement” or “exercises delegated authority to commit or bind the Department to policy decisions." The department is also looking for positions that conduct official bargaining or negotiations on behalf of the department, or whether an employee “performs statutory policy-making responsibilities." The State Department has already shifted supervisory foreign affairs officers and specialists, as well as other senior-level positions, to Schedule Policy/Career. A second State staffer said the department is still in the early stages of its expanded search for Schedule P/C conversions, but added that this work is “moving relatively fast.” Staff have been directed to update to their position descriptions to ensure they reflect the full scope of their responsibilities. “GS-13s, I don’t think, are typically in a position that you’re going to think of as a senior policymaking position,” the employee said. “I was surprised, personally, to see positions that junior given this designation.” A senior administration official told reporters in June that 97% of employees that fall under Schedule Policy/Career are at a GS-15 level or higher. The official said a “small number” of GS-13 and GS-14 employees were also converted, but that most of them work at OMB. “Outside of OMB, there are very, very few positions that are below the level of GS-15 that are being covered,” the administration official said. “The bottom line is that almost all of these are very senior positions in the federal government.” The administration official said Schedule Policy/Career would “increase the accountability of officials who are responsible for carrying out the elected president’s policy agenda,” but would have little day-to-day impact on reclassified employees. “As long as they’re performing their job duties in a competent, professional manner, they have nothing to be afraid of,” the official said. The second State Department employee said Schedule P/C’s impact on the workforce has not yet been fully felt, but suggested that newly at-will employees may be reluctant to offer candid feedback on policy matters. “If you convert my position to a position that can be expeditiously removed, I’m going to more carefully tailor what I’m saying,” they said. “Its practical effect, I think it’s safe to assume, is that it will reduce people’s willingness to give advice or offer policy positions that are inconsistent with the direction of the administration.” A third individual said the department has started reviewing GS-13 and GS-14 positions for “possible conversion to Schedule Policy/Career.” “That process has resulted in a hold on reclassifying any of the thousands of GS-13 and 14 positions, which an office or bureau might otherwise do from time to time to align position grades with updated responsibilities,” the individual said. OPM's guidance to agencies states that many aspects of federal employment – including rules around pay, leave, benefits and reductions in force – remain unchanged for those moved to Schedule P/C. OPM also included a sample termination notice agencies may use when firing Schedule P/C employees. In the template, agencies may specify “unacceptable performance or misconduct” as justification for an employee's termination. title: Bespin Global’s AI Platform Wins Grade 1 GS Certification - thelec.net
content: The “HelpNow Agentic AI Platform v4.0,” an artificial intelligence (AI) agent platform developed by AI services and solutions company Bespin Global, has received Grade 1 Good Software (GS) certification from the Telecommunications Technology Association (TTA). ​Bespin Global plans to use the certification to strengthen its public-sector business. The company will expand direct adoption channels by registering the platform on the government’s KONEPS comprehensive shopping mall, add AI agent templates tailored to public-sector areas such as administration, welfare, and safety, and optimize the platform for the public G-Cloud environment. ​Bespin Global describes the HelpNow Agentic AI Platform as an integrated AI transformation (AX) platform for building, deploying, and operating enterprise AI agents based on generative AI. ​According to Bespin Global, the platform is based on a model-independent architecture that allows flexible use of various large language models (LLMs). It supports inference, tool integration, workflow execution, application programming interface (API) integration, and external-service calls based on the Model Context Protocol (MCP). ​Bespin Global also said the product can minimize hallucinations in generative AI and improve the accuracy and reliability of responses through its proprietary agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), few-shot training, and dynamic-prompt technologies. ​The HelpNow Agentic AI Platform has also obtained ISO/IEC 42001 certification, an international standard for artificial intelligence management systems, and has been adopted by organizations including the National Pension Service, the Ulsan Metropolitan Office of Education, and the Ministry of the Interior and Safety’s “Modu-ui Gwangjang” platform.

title: GS Global opens Houston branch to expand North American energy, infrastructure business - Korea JoongAng Daily
content: The trading company opened a Houston branch to expand steel sales and project business across North America’s energy and infrastructure sectors. GS Global opened a new branch in Houston on Tuesday to strengthen its local sales presence in North America’s energy and infrastructure markets, the company said Thursday. GS Global has previously operated its U.S. business primarily through its Los Angeles subsidiary. The new Houston branch is aimed at responding to growing demand for steel for major projects amid surging investment in energy, power and infrastructure across the United States. The branch plans to expand its business beyond steel imports and sales. It will also focus on identifying demand and supporting bids for project-based steel orders, participating in the U.S. energy industry value chain and expanding into steel-related areas such as equipment for the energy, chemical and shipbuilding industries, GS Global said. The company also seeks to strengthen collaboration with major Korean steelmakers that have operations near Houston, such as Hyundai Steel and Dongkuk Steel, while developing new business opportunities with local engineering, procurement and construction companies and steel fabricators. An opening ceremony for the Houston branch was held Tuesday. It was attended by Consulate General of Korea in Houston Lee Kyung-eun, Jindal Pipe USA President Vikas Chandra and representatives from Posco, Hyundai Steel, Korea National Oil Corporation and Hanwha Ocean. “The establishment of the Houston branch is a strategic investment aimed at expanding our direct engagement with customers in the U.S. market and strengthening our sales capabilities,” a GS Global spokesperson said. “We will solidify the foundation for sustainable growth in North America by pursuing new business opportunities across a range of areas, including project-based steel sales.” Chey Tae-won has appealed a reduced property division award to former wife Roh Soh-yeong, though experts see limited chances of reversal. With the addition of the Houston Branch, GS Global now has 23 overseas bases in 16 countries worldwide. content: To create a seamless experience and for website quality and improvement purposes, we use cookie technologies for verification and quality purposes, to personalize the content presented, and to provide advertising that may be of specific interest to you. Learn our Privacy Policy here. Goldman Sachs plans to acquire NEOS for up to $2.25 billion, gaining access to 19 ETFs and $30 billion in assets under management (AUM). This move strengthens its positioning in Bitcoin and Ethereum options income strategies, distinguishing it from traditional spot ETFs. According to Woofun AI, Goldman Sachs (GS.US) officially announced an acquisition agreement with NEOS on August 12, marking a strategic shift for the Wall Street giant from simple crypto asset custody to a complex options-based business platform. The core of this transaction is not merely acquiring a cryptocurrency fund, but rather integrating NEOS's mature options ecosystem to build a comprehensive yield-generation system covering both traditional financial assets and digital assets. As the agreement was made public, market focus quickly shifted from the transaction amount itself to how Goldman Sachs plans to combine its vast client base with NEOS's unique options yield strategies to open new growth curves in the increasingly competitive ETF market. The financial structure of the deal is highly conditional and incentive-driven, with the acquisition consideration capped at $2.25 billion. The payment method includes cash and equity, with portions directly linked to future performance targets and service commitments. This means that $2.25 billion represents a theoretical valuation peak rather than a fixed cost. Based on this maximum amount, the transaction's valuation multiple is approximately 7.5% of NEOS's current assets under management (AUM), a ratio that appears relatively restrained yet highly targeted within the context of financial M&A. Subject to approvals from regulators such as the SEC and other customary closing conditions, the transaction is expected to close formally in the first quarter of 2027. As a key component of the deal, NEOS co-founders Troy Kacz and Garrett Polera will be promoted to partners at Goldman Sachs Asset Management post-closing, ensuring the stability of the core strategy team. Data compiled by Woofun AI shows that NEOS currently manages 19 ETFs with total AUM of approximately $30 billion. The vast majority of these products employ active management strategies aimed at generating excess returns through options instruments. Notably, NEOS's largest products are not cryptocurrency-related funds, but rather its traditional market offerings: the S&P 500 High Income ETF (SPYI) and the Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF (QQQI). By the end of July, AUM for these two funds had surpassed $10 billion and $13 billion, respectively. The remaining product line broadly covers small-cap equities, international stocks, real estate, bonds, U.S. Treasury notes, hedging strategies, and leveraged yield products, forming a diversified traditional asset yield matrix. Beyond its traditional business, Goldman Sachs gains a series of cryptocurrency-related products with proven operational expertise through this acquisition, most notably the NEOS Bitcoin High Income ETF (BTCI). BTCI's AUM has reached approximately $1.1 billion, making it a leading product in its category. Additionally, NEOS manages the Boosted Bitcoin High Income ETF (XBCI) and the Ethereum High Income ETF (NEHI). XBCI is designed to achieve yield levels approximately 150% of those generated by BTCI's corresponding strategy, while NEHI employs a similar yield-oriented options strategy tailored to the Ethereum market. These products present a stark structural contrast to BlackRock's (BLK.US) iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT.US). IBIT adopts a simple trust structure to hold Bitcoin directly, aiming purely to reflect its price volatility, and charges a 0.25% custody fee. In contrast, BTCI takes a distinctly different path; its annual operating expense ratio is 0.99%, and it does not hold Bitcoin spot directly. Instead, it constructs exposure through complex derivatives operations. The prospectus filed by BTCI with the SEC explicitly states that its core objective is to generate substantial monthly cash income by selling options while maintaining exposure to Bitcoin's appreciation potential. Specifically, the fund constructs a synthetic covered call strategy by purchasing call options with similar strike prices and expiration dates and selling put options, thereby simulating price exposure without actually holding Bitcoin. This mechanism allows the fund to generate cash flow through the decay of options' time value and the collection of premiums when Bitcoin prices rise moderately or trade sideways. However, if Bitcoin prices surge significantly beyond the relevant strike prices, the sold call options will begin to erode the capital appreciation gains achieved through long-term investment. The SEC clearly defines this approach as a "synthetic covered call strategy," the essence of which is trading part of the upside potential for deterministic monthly cash flows. Actual performance data for BTCI reveals the risk-return trade-off inherent in this strategy. As of June 30, BTCI's annualized distribution rate stood at 26.16%, while its 30-day SEC yield for the same period was 2.13%. However, the attractive high monthly distributions mask severe volatility in net asset value (NAV). Data shows that as of June 30, BTCI's one-year NAV total return, adjusted for distributions, was -40.9%. Bloomberg data shared by Eric Balchunas on August 11 further confirmed that, even accounting for subsequent market fluctuations, the loss over the one-year period remained approximately 42.5%. Although the fund distributes substantial cash to investors on a monthly basis, it cannot avoid a significant erosion of the overall principal. NEOS explains that these distributions are classified as return of capital for tax purposes, and their composition may include option premiums, dividends, capital gains, and interest. While this tax treatment of return of capital may offer certain tax advantages to investors, such as lowering the cost basis of the stock and thereby affecting the amount of gain or loss recognized upon future sale, it also means that the ostensibly high distribution rate does not accurately reflect actual investment performance. For U.S. investors, understanding the erosive effect of return of capital on the cost basis is crucial, as it directly impacts final after-tax returns. Unlike spot ETFs, BTCI’s return structure focuses more on generating regular cash flows rather than fully tracking every price rebound of Bitcoin. When Bitcoin prices surge sharply, the upside potential forgone by BTCI through selling call options may far exceed the income generated from the option strategy, causing its performance to lag significantly behind the spot price. Conversely, in market environments where Bitcoin prices move sideways or rise moderately, the advantages of the option strategy become apparent; even if call options expire without significant price appreciation, the premiums generated provide important support to final returns. However, this does not mean that sideways movement guarantees profitability; option pricing, holding costs, and minor fluctuations in the underlying asset price still exert complex influences on fund performance. More critically, BTCI remains exposed to the risk of declining Bitcoin prices. Its Bitcoin-related exposure shrinks as the market falls, and the hedging effect provided by call options is limited. In the event of a sharp market correction, option premiums accumulated over months could be wiped out instantly. BTCI’s performance over the past year is a typical example of this downside risk materializing rapidly; while investors enjoy high distributions, they must bear the cost of significant principal erosion. Goldman Sachs’ acquisition of NEOS is a key step in deepening its layout of option-based income products, rather than an isolated event. Goldman Sachs has already accumulated extensive experience with GPIX and GPIQ ETFs, which combine exposure to S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 assets with actively managed call option strategies, demonstrating its ability to generate income through options in traditional markets. In April this year, Goldman Sachs completed the acquisition of Innovator Capital Management, acquiring 171 fixed-income ETFs and approximately $31 billion in assets under management, showcasing its strategic preference for rapidly expanding its ETF footprint through mergers and acquisitions. The acquisition of NEOS brings Goldman Sachs an additional 19 operating ETFs with approximately $30 billion in assets under management, along with a professional team possessing mature products and strategies. Compared to launching new products from scratch and gradually building scale, directly acquiring mature products allows for rapid capture of market share. Market trends indicate that asset managers are increasingly utilizing option instruments to combine traditional asset exposure with monthly income, fixed buffer mechanisms, and leverage effects. The focus of competition has shifted from lowest-cost index tracking to the design of higher value-added income structures. A similar trend has emerged in the cryptocurrency sector: BlackRock launched its own Bitcoin premium income ETF in June, while Goldman Sachs filed an application for its proprietary Bitcoin premium income ETF in April. NEOS provides Goldman Sachs with live Bitcoin and Ethereum income products that already have a certain asset scale, enabling immediate entry into this fast-growing market segment. The first wave of spot Bitcoin ETFs addressed a fundamental question: How can investors gain Bitcoin exposure through brokerage accounts? Products like BTCI raise a deeper question: What role should this Bitcoin exposure actually play? Options can convert volatility into cash distributions, limit investors’ upside participation during price rebounds, increase leverage, or create more specific income structures. Although the ticker symbols for these products still reference Bitcoin, investors are no longer simply purchasing Bitcoin exposure, which alters the due diligence requirements investors must fulfill. For option-based cryptocurrency ETFs, understanding how income is constituted, its tax implications, and potential downside risks is as important as understanding the underlying assets. Through this acquisition, Goldman Sachs has not only acquired products but also gained the authority to define the investment logic for this emerging asset class. This move aims to propel Goldman Sachs to become the world's eighth-largest ETF manager through the acquisition of Innovator Capital Management, thereby reshaping the landscape of crypto asset allocation. According to Woofun AI, Goldman Sachs (GS.US) has officially reached an agreement to acquire NEOS Investments, an exchange-traded fund (ETF) management company, in an all-cash deal valued at up to $2.25 billion. This strategic move directly targets the crypto-asset sector, aiming to integrate NEOS’s Bitcoin- and Ethereum-related fund products into Goldman Sachs’ expanding ETF business landscape, thereby deepening its presence in the financialization of digital assets. NEOS Investments’ core assets lie in its unique option-strategy product line. The firm currently manages 19 options-based income ETFs, with total assets under management (AUM) reaching $30 billion. Its flagship products include the Bitcoin High Income ETF (BTCI.US), the Enhanced Bitcoin High Income ETF (XBCI.US), and the Ethereum High Income ETF (NEHI.US). Rather than simply tracking price fluctuations, these cryptocurrency funds employ complex option structures to provide investors with monthly fixed income streams alongside exposure to Bitcoin or Ethereum returns, thereby meeting market demand for stable cash flows. Data compiled by Woofun AI indicates that such structured products have demonstrated strong appeal in the current market environment, serving as a key driver behind NEOS’s rapid expansion. Subject to final regulatory approval, the transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. At that time, NEOS co-founders Troy Katz and Garrett Paolella, along with most of their employees, will join Goldman Sachs Asset Management. Goldman Sachs noted that, combined with its previous acquisition of Innovator Capital Management, its global ETF AUM will rise to approximately $130 billion, positioning it as the eighth-largest active ETF manager globally. Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas described this as a "surprising move," highlighting NEOS’s rapid growth since its establishment in 2022 and Goldman Sachs’ aggressive strategy of acquiring two specialized firms within a short period. Notably, this large-scale acquisition comes against the backdrop of Goldman Sachs’ recent adjustments to its crypto holdings. In the first quarter, Goldman Sachs reduced its disclosed positions in cryptocurrency ETFs, specifically by selling funds related to Ripple and Solana, while also lowering its exposure to Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs. Despite the reduction, the bank reported holding Bitcoin ETF assets worth over $700 million at the end of the quarter. This strategic shift from direct holdings to indirectly expanding influence through the acquisition of specialized management platforms marks a deeper evolution in the crypto-asset allocation logic of traditional financial giants.
